questions.stem: At Fernway, the lakehouse table holds over 100,000 small files. Which command rewrites them into fewer, larger files?
questions.explanation: OPTIMIZE compacts small files into larger ones, which speeds up reads. VACUUM removes files no longer referenced by the table.

options.text: A way to sort pipeline activities
A write-time optimization of Parquet files that makes reads faster across Fabric engines

questions.explanation: V-Order reorganizes the Parquet layout when files are written (row-group distribution, encoding and compression), so Fabric engines read them faster. The files stay standard Parquet.

questions.stem: What does VACUUM do to a Delta table?

options.text: It deletes data files no longer referenced by the table and older than the retention period, which limits time travel to that period
It deletes the table's history and data

questions.explanation: VACUUM frees storage by removing old, unreferenced files. Time travel to versions that needed those files stops working. The default retention is seven days.

questions.stem: Most queries on a large lakehouse table filter on DeviceId. Which option can improve data skipping for those queries when you optimize the table?
questions.explanation: Z-ordering co-locates related values in the same files, so filters on DeviceId can skip more files.
